anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Row-count and data-distribution statistics are stale, missing, or inaccurate, driving systematic cardinality misestimates and sub-optimal execution-plan choices.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions acquire incompatible locks on the same resources, causing blocking chains or deadlocks that stall or abort transactions.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Physical read/write demand exceeds the bandwidth or IOPS that the underlying storage can deliver, inflating I/O latency and queue depth.

When all three root causes arise together, the database exhibits a compound failure pattern: bad statistics make the optimizer favor full scans, hash joins, or broad index ranges that inflate the physical I/O footprint. The resulting surge of page reads and log writes pushes the storage subsystem beyond its throughput limits, lengthening every I/O. Statements and transactions therefore hold row, page, and metadata locks far longer than usual, causing long blocker-waiter chains, frequent deadlocks, and application timeouts. Meanwhile, auto-update statistics jobs and user-initiated ANALYZE commands are themselves delayed by lock waits and slow I/O, so the statistics remain stale, plans stay poor, and the cycle perpetuates. Symptom telemetry shows extreme divergence between estimated and actual rows, soaring PAGEIOLATCH/WRITELOG or comparable wait classes, lock and deadlock graphs growing in width and depth, and CPU trending moderate because execution is throttled by I/O and lock waits rather than computation.

Causally, inaccurate statistics start the chain by producing plans that overrun the storage system; saturated I/O then stretches lock hold times, directly amplifying contention in a transactional workload. In turn, heavy blocking prevents timely statistics collection and keeps I/O-intensive maintenance or checkpoint activities queued, which sustains the storage bottleneck. Each anomaly thus reinforces the others, driving a feedback loop that degrades throughput and undermines both concurrency control and optimizer accuracy.

entry.official_definition: Write timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol write operation exceeds mysqlx_write_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network write operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
